Simulate a series with a known trend and cycle

Source: R/simulate.R
mhp_simulate.Rd

mhp_simulate() generates a series \(x_t = g_t + c_t\) from the data generating process of Hanif, Iqbal and Choudhary (2017, eqs. 10a and 10b), after Harvey and Jaeger (1993) and Guay and St-Amant (2005): a random walk trend with drift and an AR(2) cycle, $$g_t = \mu + \tau_t + g_{t-1} + \varepsilon_t, \qquad c_t = \phi_1 c_{t-1} + \phi_2 c_{t-2} + \delta_t,$$ with \(\varepsilon_t \sim N(0, \sigma_\varepsilon^2)\) and \(\delta_t \sim N(0, \sigma_\delta^2)\). Quarterly series can be aggregated to annual ones as in the paper.

Usage

mhp_simulate(
  T = 200L,
  sd_ratio = 1,
  ar = c(1.2, -0.4),
  sd_cycle = 1,
  drift = 0.5,
  trend = c("linear", "nonlinear"),
  aggregate = c("none", "systematic", "sum", "average"),
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

T

number of (quarterly) observations (default 200, as in the paper).

sd_ratio

\(\sigma_\varepsilon / \sigma_\delta\) (default 1).

ar

\((\phi_1, \phi_2)\) of the cycle, stationary (default c(1.2, -0.4)).

sd_cycle

\(\sigma_\delta\) (default 1).

drift

\(\mu\) (default 0.5).

trend

"linear" (default) or "nonlinear".

aggregate

"none" (default), "systematic", "sum" or "average".

seed

seed of the random numbers (NULL: the current state).

Value

A data.table with the columns t, x, trend, cycle.

Details

The paper does not give the drift \(\mu\) or the form of the nonlinear trend term \(\tau_t\). Here \(\tau_t = 0\) for trend = "linear", and \(\tau_t = \mu\sin(2\pi t/T)\) for trend = "nonlinear", a drift that rises and falls once over the sample. The cycle starts from a burn-in of 100 values. Aggregation to annual data takes every fourth value ("systematic"), the sum of four consecutive values ("sum") or their average ("average"), for the series and both components.

References

Guay, A. and St-Amant, P. (2005). Do the Hodrick-Prescott and Baxter-King filters provide a good approximation of business cycles? Annales d'Economie et de Statistique, 77, 133–155. doi:10.2307/20079119

Harvey, A. C. and Jaeger, A. (1993). Detrending, stylized facts and the business cycle. Journal of Applied Econometrics, 8(3), 231–247. doi:10.1002/jae.3950080302

See also

mhp_designs, fmhp_simulation

Author

Muhammad Yaseen (myaseen208@gmail.com)

Examples

s <-
  mhp_simulate(
      T         = 200
    , sd_ratio  = 1
    , ar        = c(1.2, -0.4)
    , sd_cycle  = 1
    , drift     = 0.5
    , trend     = "linear"
    , aggregate = "none"
    , seed      = 1
    )
s
